correctness.rationale: For every \(q\ge2\), two injective two-coordinate projections have images \(P,S\) each of size \(m\). At least \(2m-q^2\) half-blocks occur in both; a word may not have both halves in this intersection because it would be a middle splice, so \(2|P\cap S|\le m\). Thus \(3m\le2q^2\). For \(q=3\), 72 admissible singleton words and all compatible codeword sets are exhaustively enumerated under hereditary pruning; two separately implemented standard-library-only programs agree on histogram 72, 1410, 7398, 9042, 1548, no sixth codeword, and 129 symmetry orbits all of size 12. Example five-word code verified directly.

value.rationale: The capacity of comma-free codes subject to aligned one-substitution correction is a natural joint synchronization/error-control problem. The projection argument gives a nonroutine one-third reduction from the unrestricted Singleton bound \(q^2\) to \(\lfloor2q^2/3\rfloor\), while the complete ternary optimum and its symmetry classification establish every best codebook at the first four-letter instance. This is a motivated exact design theorem, not a routine numeric check.
